To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HAdV-C 6 is more relevant than HAdV- C5 as a challenge virus for the hamster model and that valgancyclovir and to a lesser degree cidofovir can be used to effectively treat respiratory and intravenous HAdv- C 6 infections in the hamsters.

the hamster model of adenovirus infection can be used to evaluate the activity of antiviral drugs against both respiratory and systemic infections, and that valgancilcovir is a more effective drug for treatment of systemic infections than cidofovir.

the Syrian hamster model can be used to assess the efficacy of drugs against respiratory adenoviruses, and that valgancyclovir, and to a smaller extent cidofovir, are efficacious against adenovirus infections when administered prophylactically, or therapeutically in the hamster.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model for testing anti-adenoviral drugs and the evaluation of the activity of two drugs, VGCV and CDV, against respiratory and systemic adenovirus infections.
the development of a model for adenovirus infection and testing of drugs to treat the infection.
the development of animal models of adenovirus infection and testing of drugs that are active against these infections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HAdV-C-6 is more relevant than HAdV-5 to test antiviral drugs with the hamster model of adenovirus infection.
the hamster model of adenovirus infection is a useful tool to test antiviral compounds against HAdV-6 and other adenovirus types.
the Syrian hamster is an excellent animal model for the study of adenovirus pathogenesis and antiviral drug development.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HAdV-C7 is a better challenge virus than HAdV-5, and VGCV can be used to effectively treat adenovirus respiratory and systemic infections.

HAdV-C7 is a more relevant challenge virus than HAdV-5 for testing antiviral drugs with the immunosuppressed Syrian hamster model, because HAdV-C8 is filtered out by the tissue macrophages in hamsters to a lesser extent, and it has a 10 times lower LD50.
we have shown that HAdV-C7, which is more similar to the clinical isolates than HAdV-5, is the best adenovirus for testing antiviral drugs in the Syrian hamster model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hamster model is useful for testing drugs against respiratory adenovirus infection, which is a common complication in immunocompromised individuals.
HAdV-C1 and C5 are more relevant for the development of antiviruses than the previously used HAdV-C4 and C7.
HAdV-C 6 is a better challenge virus than HAdV C5 in the Syrian hamster model, as it is more relevant to human adenovirus infections and it is more permissive in the hamster.
